literal: Such was the sovereign's mourning regret for him.
idiomatic: Such was the sovereign's mourning regret for him.

literal: His son Rong succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Rong succeeded.

literal: Fang's younger brother Li, in youth through his father's appointment was Gentleman Attendant at Leisure, and with Duke of Xiangcheng Lu Luyuan and others served within the palace.
idiomatic: Fang's younger brother Li, in youth through his father's appointment was Gentleman Attendant at Leisure, and with Duke of Xiangcheng Lu Luyuan and others served within the palace.

literal: Respectful, keen, and talented in purpose.
idiomatic: Respectful, keen, and talented in purpose.

literal: Emperor Taiwu favored and trusted him, saying: "His father was close to my grandfather; the son at my side—is it not fitting?"
idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu favored and trusted him, saying: "His father was close to my grandfather; the son at my side—is it not fitting?"

literal: Changsun Fei
idiomatic: Changsun Fei

literal: Changsun Fei was a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Changsun Fei was a man of Dai.

literal: In the time of Zhaocheng, at age thirteen he was chosen for inner attendance.
idiomatic: In the time of Zhaocheng, at age thirteen he was chosen for inner attendance.

literal: In youth he had refined bearing, was resolute and spoke little.
idiomatic: In youth he had refined bearing, was resolute and spoke little.

literal: When Emperor Daowu was among the Dugu and Helan tribes, Fei constantly attended and followed, guarding against insult at his side; the emperor deeply trusted and relied on him.
idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu was among the Dugu and Helan tribes, Fei constantly attended and followed, guarding against insult at his side; the emperor deeply trusted and relied on him.

literal: At the beginning of Dengguo he, with Mo Ti and others, were all great generals and repeatedly won military merit.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Dengguo he, with Mo Ti and others, were all great generals and repeatedly won military merit.

literal: Later he followed in the pacification of Zhongshan and for merit was granted the title Duke of Langye.
idiomatic: Later he followed in the pacification of Zhongshan and for merit was granted the title Duke of Langye.

literal: He was transferred to Minister Steward and his title changed to Marquis of Luxiang.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister Steward and his title changed to Marquis of Luxiang.

literal: At that time the Administrator of Zhongshan, Qiu Ru, was unwilling to move inward; he fled and hid in Zhao commandery and set up Zhao Zhun as leader.
idiomatic: At that time the Administrator of Zhongshan, Qiu Ru, was unwilling to move inward; he fled and hid in Zhao commandery and set up Zhao Zhun as leader.

literal: He falsely made demonic words saying: "Yan tilts east; Zhao shall continue.
idiomatic: He falsely made demonic words saying: "Yan tilts east; Zhao shall continue.

literal: If you wish to know his name, the Huai River is not enough.
idiomatic: If you wish to know his name, the Huai River is not enough.

literal: " Zhun gladly followed him, styled himself Duke of Julu, and Ru served as Chief Clerk.
idiomatic: " Zhun gladly followed him, styled himself Duke of Julu, and Ru served as Chief Clerk.

literal: They held Guan city, linked in the Dingling, and killed the chief officials.
idiomatic: They held Guan city, linked in the Dingling, and killed the chief officials.

literal: Fei defeated Zhun at Jiumen, beheaded Qiu Ru, and captured Zhun alive.
idiomatic: Fei defeated Zhun at Jiumen, beheaded Qiu Ru, and captured Zhun alive.

literal: An edict ordered that Ru's flesh be used to feed Zhun; he was sent to the capital, broken on the wheel at the market, and his clan exterminated.
idiomatic: An edict ordered that Ru's flesh be used to feed Zhun; he was sent to the capital, broken on the wheel at the market, and his clan exterminated.

literal: Fei was appointed Inspector of Yan Province.
idiomatic: Fei was appointed Inspector of Yan Province.

idiomatic: When Yao Ping raided Pingyang, Emperor Daowu campaigned and made Fei, with Prince of Piling Shun and others, the vanguard.

literal: Ping retreated to hold Chaiwall; the emperor advanced and stormed it.
idiomatic: Ping retreated to hold Chaiwall; the emperor advanced and stormed it.

literal: He sent Fei back to garrison Yan Province and comfort Henan; his prestige and trust were manifest on the Huai and Si.
idiomatic: He sent Fei back to garrison Yan Province and comfort Henan; his prestige and trust were manifest on the Huai and Si.

literal: Skilled in stratagem, his courage topped the generals.
idiomatic: Skilled in stratagem, his courage topped the generals.

literal: In campaigns before and after, he never once failed.
idiomatic: In campaigns before and after, he never once failed.

literal: Therefore whenever there was great peril they put Fei in charge;
idiomatic: Therefore whenever there was great peril they put Fei in charge;

literal: in pacifying the central plains southward and crushing Qiang raiders westward, Fei's merit was greatest; rewards numbered in the thousands.
idiomatic: in pacifying the central plains southward and crushing Qiang raiders westward, Fei's merit was greatest; rewards numbered in the thousands.

literal: Later his title was reduced to Marquis of Lantian.
idiomatic: Later his title was reduced to Marquis of Lantian.

idiomatic: He died; posthumous name Wu, buried with honor at Jinling.

literal: His son Han succeeded to the title.
idiomatic: His son Han succeeded to the title.

literal: Han in youth had his father's manner.
idiomatic: Han in youth had his father's manner.

literal: Under Emperor Daowu, for skill in mounted archery he was made Hunt Officer.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Daowu, for skill in mounted archery he was made Hunt Officer.

literal: When Mingyuan was abroad, Han with Yuan Mohun and others secretly plotted to welcome and install him.
idiomatic: When Mingyuan was abroad, Han with Yuan Mohun and others secretly plotted to welcome and install him.

literal: When Mingyuan took the throne, he and Mohun and others attended to remonstrance at the emperor's side.
idiomatic: When Mingyuan took the throne, he and Mohun and others attended to remonstrance at the emperor's side.

literal: For merit he was repeatedly promoted to General Who Pacifies the South.
idiomatic: For merit he was repeatedly promoted to General Who Pacifies the South.

literal: He led troops to garrison the northern frontier; his martial renown was very great.
idiomatic: He led troops to garrison the northern frontier; his martial renown was very great.

literal: When Emperor Taiwu took the throne, he was enfeoffed Prince of Pingyang.
idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu took the throne, he was enfeoffed Prince of Pingyang.

literal: When the Rouran khan Datan invaded Yunzhong, Emperor Taiwu campaigned in person.
idiomatic: When the Rouran khan Datan invaded Yunzhong, Emperor Taiwu campaigned in person.

literal: He sent Han with Duke of Dongping E Qing out of Changchuan to attack Datan.
idiomatic: He sent Han with Duke of Dongping E Qing out of Changchuan to attack Datan.

literal: Datan fled north; they pursued, struck, captured booty, and returned.
idiomatic: Datan fled north; they pursued, struck, captured booty, and returned.

literal: He was transferred to Minister of Education.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Education.

literal: He followed in the assault on Helian Chang and defeated him.
idiomatic: He followed in the assault on Helian Chang and defeated him.

literal: Han was upright, pure, and strict and bright; he delighted in comforting officers and soldiers; when he died, Emperor Taiwu wept for him and came in person to his mourning.
idiomatic: Han was upright, pure, and strict and bright; he delighted in comforting officers and soldiers; when he died, Emperor Taiwu wept for him and came in person to his mourning.

literal: Mourning rites followed the precedent of Prince of Ancheng Shusun Jun.
idiomatic: Mourning rites followed the precedent of Prince of Ancheng Shusun Jun.

literal: Posthumous name Wei, buried with honor at Jinling.
idiomatic: Posthumous name Wei, buried with honor at Jinling.

literal: His son Cheng succeeded to the title, reduced to duke, and held the post of Director of the Southern Department.
idiomatic: His son Cheng succeeded to the title, reduced to duke, and held the post of Director of the Southern Department.

literal: He died, buried with honor at Jinling.
idiomatic: He died, buried with honor at Jinling.

literal: Han's younger brother Ling held the post of Director of the Imperial Stud.
idiomatic: Han's younger brother Ling held the post of Director of the Imperial Stud.

literal: By nature generous and broad; he loved learning and cherished scholars.
idiomatic: By nature generous and broad; he loved learning and cherished scholars.

literal: Enfeoffed Duke of Wu commandery, posthumously made Prince of Wu commandery.
idiomatic: Enfeoffed Duke of Wu commandery, posthumously made Prince of Wu commandery.

literal: Posthumous name Gong, buried with honor at Jinling.
idiomatic: Posthumous name Gong, buried with honor at Jinling.

literal: Discussion says: At the end of Zhaocheng, the multitudes rebelled and kin turned away.
idiomatic: The commentators say: At the end of Zhaocheng, subjects rebelled and kin turned away.

literal: Changsun Song was generous, deep, and resolute, bearing the weight of the royal house, serving through many reigns, remote as a founding elder.
idiomatic: Changsun Song was generous, deep, and resolute, bearing the weight of the royal house, serving through many reigns, remote as a founding elder.

literal: Alive he was a pillar minister; dead he is sacrificed in the clear temple—beautiful!
idiomatic: In life a pillar of the state; in death honored in the clear temple—how fine!

literal: Jian's capacity and insight were bright and fair, his stratagems penetrating and ample; towering, he had the look of a chief minister; stern and upright, he had a king's minister's integrity.
idiomatic: Jian's capacity and insight were bright and fair, his stratagems penetrating and ample; towering, he had the look of a chief minister; stern and upright, he had a king's minister's integrity.

literal: Yet his days in the court were few and his days on the frontier many—why?
idiomatic: Yet why were his days at court so few and his days on the frontier so many?

literal: Ping's knowledge was comprehensive and penetrating; within and without his fame flowed; taken from opening things and completing tasks, he was perhaps also a rafter beam for Sui.
idiomatic: Ping's knowledge was comprehensive and penetrating; within and without his fame flowed; taken from opening things and completing tasks, he was perhaps also a rafter beam for Sui.

literal: Daosheng was respectful, cautious, frugal, and restrained, and together bore a martial name; known to a bright lord, his voice entered song and performance.
idiomatic: Daosheng was respectful, cautious, frugal, and restrained, and together bore a martial name; known to a bright lord, his voice entered song and performance.

literal: The two dukes stood side by side, their brilliance dazzling court and countryside; their house's blessing and hereditary salary, glory covering later generations.
idiomatic: The two dukes stood side by side, their brilliance dazzling court and countryside; their house's blessing and hereditary salary, glory covering later generations.

literal: Though the eight kings of Han cannot match their lush achievements;
idiomatic: Though the eight kings of Han cannot match their lush achievements;

literal: the seven generations of the Zhang clan cannot compare with this doubled glory.
idiomatic: the seven generations of the Zhang clan cannot compare with this doubled glory.

literal: Ziyan's courage and fierceness were unmatched; Shaoyuan's music was uniquely subtle;
idiomatic: Ziyan's courage and fierceness were unmatched; Shaoyuan's music was uniquely subtle;

literal: Chi was early hailed as outstanding; Lan alone excelled in bold eloquence.
idiomatic: Chi was early hailed as outstanding; Lan alone excelled in bold eloquence.

literal: Otherwise how could they together command armies, jointly oversee the ritual offices, bells and tripods not fallen—and be both duke and marquis?
idiomatic: Otherwise how could they together command armies, jointly oversee the ritual offices, bells and tripods not fallen—and be both duke and marquis?

literal: Sheng's person combined heroic martial bearing and embraced singular stratagems.
idiomatic: Sheng's person combined heroic martial bearing and embraced singular stratagems.

literal: Seizing the moment he made changes, cherishing those frontier tribes—their nests overturned and all fell, knees bent and foreheads touched the ground.
idiomatic: He seized the moment and adapted; he turned on those frontier tribes—their nests overturned and all fell, knees bent and foreheads to the ground.

literal: On the border ramparts the clanging arrow-travel ceased; at the Wei Bridge there was the single chieftain's bow.
idiomatic: On the border ramparts the whistling arrows fell silent; at the Wei Bridge a chieftain bowed in submission.

literal: His grace flowed to the northern frontier; his merit lit the royal house— to preserve this hereditary salary, was it not fitting!
idiomatic: His grace flowed to the northern frontier; his merit lit the royal house— to preserve this hereditary salary, was it not fitting!

literal: Fei bound his hair and served within the palace; by martial prowess he stood on his own; wherever his army's edge pointed, none failed to scatter and flee—Guan and Zhang at ten thousand men apiece are not worth counting many.
idiomatic: Fei bound his hair and served in the inner palace; by martial prowess he stood alone; wherever his army's edge pointed, foes scattered—Guan and Zhang, each a match for ten thousand, are hardly worth extra praise.

literal: Han had his father's manner and did not ruin the ancestral structure; extra rites at the mourning—there was reason for it!
idiomatic: Han had his father's manner and did not ruin the ancestral house; the emperor's added rites at his mourning—there was cause for that.
